findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. the link is forwarded/shared, or the user follows `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` for a topic they never interacted with, or a notification was generated without creating a TopicUser). The next line `if tu.notification_level > ...` dereferences nil and raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 to the user instead of handling the case. The action should guard against a missing TopicUser (create one via `TopicUser.change`, or treat it as already-unsubscribed).

findings.title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
findings.body: The action mutates `tu` and calls `tu.save!` directly instead of using `TopicUser.change`. As a result: `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated (so the topic's notification reason stays e.g. `auto_watch_category`, which is why the client route has to null out `notificationReasonText` to hide it), no `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... })` is sent (other open tabs/clients keep showing the old state), and `observe_after_save_callbacks_for`/UserActionObserver are not run. The unsubscribe should go through `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)` so the same bookkeeping as the rest of the app happens.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking emails that don't pass it
findings.body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` string was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` in addition to `%{user_preferences_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` render `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every message built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url:`; any other path that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url:` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` while building the message. The existing spec had to add `unsubscribe_url:` for exactly this reason. Either supply a default `unsubscribe_url` in `MessageBuilder#initialize`, or make the interpolation tolerant.

findings.title: Template name does not match the topicUnsubscribe route
findings.body: The route is declared as `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' })` and has no custom `renderTemplate`/`templateName`. Ember therefore looks up the default template for route name `topicUnsubscribe` (i.e. `topic-unsubscribe`), matching the added controller and view files which use the dashed name. The template added here is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which resolves to the template name `topic/unsubscribe` (the form used for a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route). With the current route name this template will not be found, so the unsubscribe route renders no template (blank page). Rename the file to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs` or provide an explicit `renderTemplate`/`templateName`.

findings.title: Unsubscribe mutates state via a GET request with no CSRF protection
findings.body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level but is reachable through the GET routes `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`, and the action is added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`. Rails does not apply the CSRF token check to GET requests, so a third-party page can embed `` and, for a logged-in user, silently mute that topic without their consent. The same GET also makes the action vulnerable to link prefetching/scanning by clients that try to follow links. State-changing actions reached from emails should use a confirm step or a signed/tokenized request rather than a bare GET.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe behavior
findings.body: The only spec change is adding `unsubscribe_url:` to an existing message-builder example; nothing asserts the new behavior. There are no specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (including the nil-TopicUser case and the redirect when slug is blank), the new `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` / `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` routes, `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, or the fact that the per-topic link actually appears in the rendered email body/HTML. Given the action contains a crash path and bypasses the normal `TopicUser.change` path, these paths need coverage before merge.
